props.gloss_en: the mishna: a person may take a hammer to crack nuts with it
Rav Yehuda: [the mishna's hammer is] a nut-hammer, to crack nuts with it -- but a blacksmiths' hammer, no
a thing whose function is prohibited is forbidden [to move] even for its own use
the mishna's seifa: [one may take] the winnowing shovel and the pitchfork to place [food] on it for a child
Rabba: [the mishna's hammer is] a blacksmiths' hammer, to crack nuts with it
a thing whose function is prohibited is permitted [to move] for its own use
a mortar: if there is garlic in it, one may move it
and if not, one may not move it
Rabba: whose is this [ruling on the mortar]? It is R' Nechemya's

and Beit Hillel permit

Rav: since one is particular about them, he designates a place for them
Rabba: this [pestle] too -- one designates a place for it

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה, סיפא דקתני ואת הרחת ואת המלגז לתת עליו לקטן -- רחת ומלגז מי מייחדי ליה לקטן?! -- the seifa permits tools not designated for the use, so the reisha's hammer need not be a nut-hammer
איתיביה אביי לרבה: an empty mortar may not be moved -- a vessel whose function is prohibited is forbidden even for another use

answered_by.gloss_en: הא מני -- רבי נחמיה היא, דאמר אין כלי ניטל אלא לצורך תשמישו (= p_medocha_r_nechemya)

objections.gloss_en: איתיביה: ושוין שאם קיצב עליו בשר שאסור לטלטלו -- even Beit Hillel forbid moving the pestle afterwards, so a vessel whose function is prohibited is forbidden for another use

answered_by.gloss_en: having heard Rav's הכל מודים בסיכי זיירי ומזורי: הא נמי מייחד להו מקום -- the pestle, like the launderers' pins, has a designated place, so all agree it is not moved (= p_eli_meyached_makom)
